rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
prompt: ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Polish forest spirit, Boruta appearing as a black dog. ANATOMY: one natural-sized black dog, one head, two natural eyes, four canine legs, one tail, coarse wet black fur, no horns, glowing eyes, extra anatomy or human clothes. MOMENT: Confront the camera at close distance, snarl and deliberately rake a mushroom-and-berry basket from a confused traveller's hands, scattering its contents across the narrow forest dyke as the traveller is drawn off the good path. POWER: The documented forest spirit spills gathered mushrooms and berries and leads people astray; only ordinary physical contact and scattered berries, no supernatural energy. SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle; subject fills frame, natural documented size, never unsupported gigantic. LIGHT & WEATHER: one warm lateral source, deep shadows, crisp rim, physically moving dust/water only. SURFACE: tactile coarse textures, rich walnut/antique-gold palette. SETTING: night in Polish pine woods and a narrow earthen dyke by dry willows, wrong twisting path beyond, a human traveller behind establishes normal dog scale. MOOD: dangerous or awe-inspiring, never ordinary, cute, calm or decorative. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, symbols, logos, border, signature, watermark; no extra heads or limbs; no franchises; no nudity, transparent clothes, blood, wounds or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon lines or energy ribbons.
